meta.description: Deming’s documented sentence is longer and ends the other way: “But to survive, we must learn.” The punchy short form has no traced source.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Learning is not compulsory... neither is survival'?
meta.ogDescription: Wikiquote’s sourced Deming line reads “But to survive, we must learn.” “Neither is survival” is a later compression with no identified source.

answer.label: Not Deming’s words — a compressed paraphrase
answer.sourceLine: The thought is Deming’s; the sentence is not. The wording that can actually be documented — transcribed by Frank Voehl from his own recording of Deming’s 4-Day Seminar at Newport Beach, California, 24–28 February 1986, and printed in his 1995 volume Deming: The Way We Knew Him — is longer and lands the other way: “Learning is not compulsory; it’s voluntary… But to survive, we must learn.” Wikiquote attaches a note ↗ to that sourced entry saying the quote “is often cited as ‘Learning is not compulsory... neither is survival.’”

source.heading: The nearest documented wording

docMeta.dd: Deming: The Way We Knew Him
CRC Press / St. Lucie Press, 28 February 1995 (ISBN 1884015549)

source.excerpt: Learning is not compulsory; it’s voluntary. Improvement is not compulsory; it’s voluntary. But to survive, we must learn. The penalty for ignorance is that you get beat up. There is no substitute for knowledge. Yet time is of the essence.
trail: 1986–1993 — Deming publishes his two major books, Out of the Crisis (1986) ↗ and The New Economics (1993). A full-text search of each returns no instance of “compulsory” and none of “neither is survival” — whatever he said about learning and survival, he did not put it in print.

24–28 February 1986 — Deming teaches his 4-Day Seminar “Quality Productivity, and Competitive Position” at Newport Beach, California, and Frank Voehl records it. The W. Edwards Deming Institute ↗ cites that personal recording as the source of the sentence — a contemporaneous record made seven years before Deming died, not a memory reconstructed afterwards.
20 December 1993 — Deming dies in Washington, D.C. at 93, per his Wikipedia biography ↗.
1995 — Frank Voehl’s Deming: The Way We Knew Him puts the transcribed sentence into print on page 125 ↗: “Learning is not compulsory; it’s voluntary… But to survive, we must learn.”

Since then — the line circulates in a shorter, punchier form. Wikiquote ↗ keeps the sourced version and adds a flat note: this quote “is often cited as ‘Learning is not compulsory... neither is survival.’”
source.excerptNote: Reconstructed from Google Books search-inside snippets for page 125, which begin mid-page. The words are Deming’s, recorded at the February 1986 Newport Beach seminar and transcribed by the volume’s own author, Frank Voehl, who adds immediately after: “These words certainly haunted me for years…”

author.name: W. Edwards Deming
author.heading: Who was W. Edwards Deming?
author.bio: William Edwards Deming (born Sioux City, Iowa, 14 October 1900; died Washington, D.C., 20 December 1993) was an American statistician, engineer and management consultant whose statistical quality-control methods helped rebuild Japanese industry after the Second World War. He is best known for his 14 Points for Management and for insisting that quality problems belong to the system and its managers rather than to the workers. Much of his teaching happened out loud — in seminars rather than on the page — which is precisely why so many of his best-known lines survive as other people’s recollections.

misattribution.heading: What actually went wrong here
misattribution.intro: This is not a case of a quote being pinned on the wrong person. The idea is Deming’s and the setting is real — what changed is the sentence. Somewhere between a 1995 book of recollections and the modern slide deck, a three-clause thought lost its ending and gained a punchline.

items.why: The documented sentence ends “But to survive, we must learn” — survival as a condition, not an option. Wikiquote’s note ↗ records the short form only as how the sourced quote “is often cited,” not as something Deming is documented saying.

Neither wording is in his published work. A full-text search of Out of the Crisis (1986) ↗ and of The New Economics (1993) returns no instance of the word “compulsory” and none of the phrase “neither is survival.” The only documented text comes from the lecture room: Frank Voehl’s recording of the 24–28 February 1986 Newport Beach 4-Day Seminar, printed in 1995. That is why the long version is attested and the short one is not.

items.who: “In God we trust. All others must bring data.”
items.why: Deming attracts crisp aphorisms he never wrote. Quote Investigator ↗ found the earliest use in 1978 by Professor Edwin R. Fisher, who already called it a well-recognised cliché, and concluded there is “no substantive support for assigning the saying to that famous engineer.”

misattribution.truthLine: The idea is Deming’s; the epigram is the internet’s. What is on the record is “Learning is not compulsory; it’s voluntary… But to survive, we must learn,” printed on page 125 ↗ of Frank Voehl’s 1995 volume, transcribed from his own recording of a February 1986 Deming seminar.

context.heading: Why the short version travels better
lead: The compressed line is better copy than the original, which is exactly the problem. “Learning is not compulsory... neither is survival” is a closed loop with a shrug at the end: refuse to learn, accept the consequences, your call. The documented sentence does something less tidy and considerably more Deming — it sorts what is optional from what is not. Learning is voluntary. Improvement is voluntary. Survival, though, comes with a condition attached.

Frank Voehl was not reconstructing seminar language from memory — he had it on tape, and the Institute cites that tape. The internal evidence agrees: the same page-125 passage runs straight on into “There is no substitute for knowledge” — a line that Wikiquote also records ↗ from Deming’s own The New Economics (1993). The passage sounds like him because it is him, in a room, in February 1986.
context.detailsSummary: The two versions do not say the same thing
detailsBody: “Neither is survival” makes survival optional. “But to survive, we must learn” makes survival conditional. One is a joke about indifference; the other is a warning with a price attached. The compression is wittier and says less — and it is the version that ended up on ten thousand slide decks.

Deming is a heavy magnet for this kind of drift. The best-known case is “In God we trust. All others must bring data,” which Quote Investigator traced ↗ to Professor Edwin R. Fisher in 1978 — who already called it a well-recognised cliché — concluding there is “no substantive support” for assigning it to Deming.

schema.verdictNote: The popular short form “Learning is not compulsory... neither is survival” is disputed and has no identified source. What Deming is documented as saying is the longer sentence recorded here: “Learning is not compulsory; it’s voluntary. Improvement is not compulsory; it’s voluntary. But to survive, we must learn” — from a recording of his 4-Day Seminar at Newport Beach, California, 24–28 February 1986, printed in Frank Voehl’s Deming: The Way We Knew Him (1995), p. 125.
